content.user_title: Analyze Molecular Biology Data with Biopython
content.value_statement: Bioinformatics work often requires accurate parsing, database access, and reproducible analysis steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Biopython workflows for molecular biology data.
actual_capabilities: Guides reading, writing, and converting FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, PDB, and mmCIF files.
Explains Bio.Entrez workflows for NCBI searches, summaries, record fetching, and linked database records.
Shows how to run NCBI BLAST queries, save results, and parse XML or tabular BLAST output.
Covers pairwise alignments, multiple alignment files, substitution matrices, and alignment statistics.
Supports protein structure parsing, chain and residue navigation, distance calculations, and PDB export patterns.
Provides examples for phylogenetic tree reading, construction, manipulation, and visualization.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install Biopython or external bioinformatics tools automatically.
NCBI database and web BLAST examples require internet access and user-provided contact information.
Local BLAST, DSSP, MUSCLE, and similar tools must be installed separately when needed.
It does not validate biological conclusions or replace domain expert review.

use_cases.title: Process sequence datasets
use_cases.description: Parse FASTA or GenBank files, calculate sequence properties, convert formats, and stream large datasets efficiently.

use_cases.title: Retrieve NCBI records
use_cases.description: Search PubMed or GenBank, fetch records, follow related database links, and respect NCBI usage requirements.

use_cases.title: Inspect protein structures
use_cases.description: Read PDB or mmCIF files, navigate chains and residues, calculate distances, and export selected structure regions.

prompt_templates.title: Read Sequence Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to read a FASTA file with Biopython and summarize each sequence identifier, length, and description.

prompt_templates.title: Search NCBI Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search NCBI PubMed for a biology topic, fetch the first results, and explain the required Entrez settings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare BLAST Hits
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Biopython workflow that runs a BLAST search, saves the result, parses top hits, and filters them by E-value.

prompt_templates.title: Build Analysis Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible Biopython pipeline that converts GenBank records to FASTA, aligns sequences, builds a tree, and records parameters.

output_examples.input: Summarize a FASTA file with many records.
output: The response identifies the relevant SeqIO parser and format name.
It recommends streaming records one at a time for large files.
It describes a concise summary table with sequence identifiers, lengths, and descriptions.

output_examples.input: Fetch GenBank records from NCBI for a list of accessions.
output: The response explains that Entrez email is required before requests.
It outlines search or fetch steps, handle closing, and format choices.
It notes rate limits and recommends caching downloaded records.

output_examples.input: Analyze distances in a PDB protein structure.
output: The response selects Bio.PDB as the relevant module.
It explains the structure, model, chain, residue, and atom hierarchy.
It describes how to compare atom coordinates and report interpretable distances.

best_practices: Set Entrez email and respect NCBI rate limits before using online database examples.
Use iterators and streaming parsers for large biological files.
Record file formats, thresholds, database names, and tool versions for reproducible analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys or personal contact details in shared scripts.
Do not run large repeated web BLAST or Entrez requests without caching results.
Do not assume parser format names match files without checking the input format.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users apply Biopython to sequence files, NCBI databases, BLAST results, protein structures, and phylogenetic trees.

faq.question: Does it install Biopython automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples. Users must install Biopython and any external tools in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it access NCBI databases?
faq.answer: It explains Bio.Entrez access patterns. Actual access requires internet connectivity and user-provided NCBI contact settings.

faq.question: Does it support BLAST workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers web BLAST submission, local BLAST command wrappers, saved results, and XML or tabular parsing.

faq.question: Can it analyze protein structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Bio.PDB parsing, chain and residue navigation, atom distances, superimposition, and selected structure export.

faq.question: Is it suitable for very large datasets?
faq.answer: It includes streaming and caching guidance, but users must still manage memory, network limits, and local compute resources.
